extracted.intended_audience: readers and writers of natural philosophy / scientific cosmography (scientists, educated public interested in 19th-century physical description of the universe)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing a general delineation of nature (a physical cosmography): how to select scope, order material, balance observation and speculation, and present scientific description across scales. Targets authors/synthesizers summarizing contemporary astronomical and terrestrial knowledge for a learned public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency between experiment and philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: “The results yielded by an earnest investigation in the path of experiment can not be at variance with a true philosophy of nature.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a contradiction arises between experimental results and speculative philosophy, the fault lies either in unsound speculation or in empiricism that overstates what is proved by experiment. Ensure theoretical claims reconcile with experimental evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of empirical observation with rational synthesis
rubrics_metrics.description: “Science does not present itself to man until mind conquers matter in striving to subject the result of experimental investigation to rational combinations.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present observed facts not as isolated data but as subject to rational combinations — the labor of mind applied to nature. The descriptive work should connect sensory perceptions with intellectual interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resist excessive division and minute enumeration
rubrics_metrics.description: “The descriptive picture of nature which we purpose drawing must not enter too fully into detail... The delineator of nature must resist the tendency toward endless division.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid exhaustive lists and hyper-differentiation that obscure unity; focus on masses or classes that convey magnitude and relationships rather than cataloguing every empirical particular.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance austere reason with imaginative speculation
rubrics_metrics.description: “It would be a denial of the dignity of human nature... were we to condemn at one time austere reason... and at another that exercise of the imagination which prompts and excites discoveries.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not distrust generalization or speculative thought outright; allow reasoned induction and creative imagination to play complementary roles in producing insights and hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose an organizational method appropriate to purpose (near-to-far vs far-to-near)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two possible orders: begin with the terrestrial (human-interest, sense-based view) or begin with regions of space (objective cosmography) depending on whether the work is an exposition for perception or a physical cosmography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the sequence (earth-first or space-first) that matches the work’s aim: elementary/astronomical pedagogy often proceeds from apparent to real movements (near-to-far), while an exposition of established knowledge may begin with cosmic structures (far-to-near).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish exposition from formal demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: “Another course of ideas must, however, be pursued in a work which proposes merely to give an exposition of what is known... and does not enter into a consideration of the proofs on which such results have been based.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing an exposition or overview, it is acceptable to summarize results without reproducing full proofs; make clear when you are stating accepted knowledge versus deriving it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize quantification and mean numerical values
rubrics_metrics.description: “In all that is subject to motion and change in space, the ultimate aim, the very expression of physical laws, depend upon 'mean numerical values'... the progress of modern physical science is especially characterized by the attainment and rectification of the mean values of certain quantities by means of the processes of weighing and measuring.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize measurement, numerical averages, and careful quantification (weighing, measuring) as central to expressing physical laws and stabilizing variable phenomena in exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensiveness across scales while remaining selective
rubrics_metrics.description: “A picture of the world may... include the realms of infinity no less than the minute microscopic animal and vegetable organisms... All that can be perceived by the senses, and all that has been accumulated up to the present day by an attentive and variously directed study of nature, constitute the materials from which this representation is to be drawn.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to represent phenomena from cosmic to microscopic scales, but be selective in presentation to preserve clarity and unity—include salient examples rather than exhaustive catalogues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge limits of knowledge and avoid dogmatism
rubrics_metrics.description: “A considerable portion of the qualitative properties of matter... is doubtlessly still unknown to us... the attempt perfectly to represent unity in diversity must therefore necessarily prove unsuccessful.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly recognize uncertainties, the provisional nature of many conclusions, and the presence of unknowns; avoid presenting speculative conclusions as absolute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for observational limitations and instrument variability
rubrics_metrics.description: “Want of uniformity in the power of the instruments employed, different conditions of our atmosphere, and other optical relations, render a part of the results invalid as historical evidence.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When citing observational changes or historical observations, consider instrument power, atmospheric conditions, and other observational biases; be cautious in treating such reports as definitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use clear taxonomy and technical definitions (e.g., nebulae types)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinctions provided: 'nebulous stars' (part of nebulous mass surrounding a body) vs irregularly-shaped nebulous spots vs planetary nebulae (circular disks with uniform faint light).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise categories and definitions to avoid confusion when classifying astronomical phenomena; explain distinguishing observational features and possible interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ analogies (organic development) to explain cosmic formation
rubrics_metrics.description: “The genetic evolution... has led philosophical observers to the discovery of the analogy existing among organic phenomena. As in our forests we see the same kind of tree in all the various stages of its growth...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use organic-growth analogies to help readers conceptualize stages of nebular condensation and cosmic evolution, while making clear the limits of analogy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sidereal scales (star-count method) to infer spatial distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: “For the generalization of cosmical views... our starry stratum is inferred from sidereal scales, that is to say, from that method of counting the stars... based upon the equidistant subdivision of the telescopic field of view.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply systematic star counts across equal telescope fields to infer relative depth, density, and the form of starry strata; explain methodology and its assumptions when used to derive spatial structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid projecting fanciful illusions; ground descriptions in observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of how earlier philosophies and imagination produced illusive images (e.g., seeing new lands from the Canaries) and how a disciplined science must avoid such phantoms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be skeptical of seductive but untested cosmological images; favor disciplined observation and reasoned inference rather than appealing but unsupported imaginative constructs.
